newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends strong on dollar flow to bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends strong on dollar flow to bourse.

text.p: The Mexican peso ended stronger on Tuesday amid foreign capital flow into a soaring local stock market, dealers said.

"Foreigners jumped into the market today," a trader said, adding that forecast falls in domestic primary interest rates curbed additional peso strength. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed trade for the day 2.25 and 2.2 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8990/7.9025 and 7.8970/7.9000 per dollar.
The bourse's leading IPC index had gained 113.41 points to a new record of 4,854.65 in late trade.

"There were a lot of contrary bids, but the market is still very liquid (in dollars)," the trader added. "We need to see the outcome of this evening's primary auction, although we have discounted a fall of 150 basis points."
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders, taken shortly before the central bank closed bids, showed they forecast an average assigned rate of 18.56 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes.
This would be a fall of 139 basis points from last week's auction. Banco de Mexico was expected to announce auction results at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.2 centavos weaker at 7.9080/7.9110 per dollar.
Dealers said they would look carefully at inflation data for June, which the central bank was expected to release some time on Wedmnesday.
